arc: hook ("You just speak" → mic) → feature (voice pill → "Your idea") → turn ("and it builds for you") → feature (prompt box) → transition (send click flood) → feature (dashboards spiral) → transition (rings → mark) → benefit (blob writes lines, swells to logo) → logo ("this is Codex.")

scenes.title: "You just speak" glitches into a mic button
scenes.summary: On near-white, "You just" resolves out of blur in a large humanist sans, the colour settling from light blue to navy, and "speak" types in letter by letter. "speak" glitches to "sp)ak" for three frames and dissolves while a white mic button with a purple mic icon springs in where it was. A cursor glides in from the lower right, presses the mic (it tints pale blue), and the camera pushes in 3.8x onto the button.
scenes.build: BlurWord (blur + colour lerp from `from` to `to`) for each word and letter; the mic uses spring() scale; the cursor x/y come from glide() (monotone cubic spline) so it never stops dead between keys. The push-in is a <Camera> keyframe that lands on exactly the framing scene 02 opens on.
scenes.reuse: Use for a voice-input or 'just say it' hook: swap the line and have the key word morph into the UI control it describes. Keep glide() for cursor paths. The camera end framing is matched to scene 02, so retune it if used alone.

scenes.title: Mic disc stretches into a waveform pill, then "Your idea"
scenes.summary: Opening inside the 3.8x push from scene 01 (the giant word "just" to the left), the pressed mic disc stretches into a long white pill as 16 light-blue waveform bars dance beside the mic icon and a grey caption chip reads "Can you build me an app?". The pill slides away left and shrinks while "Your idea" (330px) resolves letter by letter out of blur, then slides out left blurring.
scenes.build: Disc centre and pill width are glide() curves so the drift and slide are one continuous move; the bars are divs whose height is a seeded sine per bar. The "Your idea" letters each blur in with a colour lerp via mix(); the cursor drops out of frame on a glide.
scenes.reuse: A clean voice-capture beat for any voice/dictation product: swap the caption chip text and the follow-up words. Pair it with scene 01 to keep the matched framing.

scenes.title: "and it builds for you" blur-word card
scenes.summary: A one-second line, "and it builds for you", resolves word by word out of blur at centre; "and it builds" settles to ink and "for you" stays light blue.
scenes.build: Five BlurWord spans with staggered starts in a flex row. Nothing else.
scenes.reuse: A bridge line; use BlurWord directly rather than this file.

scenes.title: Glass prompt box over a meadow loop, prompt suffix swaps
scenes.summary: Out of a cyan-washed blur, a looping meadow-and-sea video settles behind "What should we work on?" and a frosted glass prompt pill (plus icon, "5.5 Medium" model picker, mic, white send button). "Build me a website" types in; the camera punches in 2.5x onto the prompt with zoom blur and depth of field, and the ending swaps "a website" → "an app" → "a tool" as a motion-blurred cursor sweeps an arc beneath it and exits right toward send. Edges stretch in and out through a pincushion lens.
scenes.build: Fisheye (SVG feDisplacementMap with an inlined radial map; invert = pincushion) wraps a <Camera> with keyframes mirrored in camAt() so zoom blur is sized to actual zoom speed. Suffix spans crossfade each ending; MotionCursor follows a splinePath (Catmull-Rom in time) and turns to face travel with directional blur. Background is a <Video> loop.
scenes.reuse: The go-to 'type a prompt into an AI app' shot: swap TYPED, the three suffixes, the model label and the background video. Fisheye, MotionCursor and splinePath are reusable components. Don't copy the Codex-specific '5.5 Medium' label.

scenes.title: Extreme close-up cursor click on send, flood to white
scenes.summary: An extreme close-up of the prompt pill's right end over a blurred meadow: the huge send arrow button slides in and settles while a big cursor sweeps in from the left, dips under the mic and curves up onto the button. It clicks (button presses and tints blue), then the shot pushes in 7x exponentially and floods to near-white.
scenes.build: MotionCursor with an `anchor` so the cursor rides the panning button without counting the pan as its own motion, plus a time-ramped faceWeight so it settles into a resting lean instead of snapping. The press is a sine; zoom = exp(log(7) * push) so it accelerates smoothly from rest.
scenes.reuse: Use as the 'hit send / start' cut into a results scene; swap the button icon and background. The anchored cursor and exponential push are the techniques to take.

scenes.title: Finished app screenshots spiral out of the centre
scenes.summary: On pale blue-white, six cards spiral out of the frame centre as blue-violet gradient placeholders and resolve into finished app screenshots (CRM, crypto, Pulseboard, BriefBot, overview dashboards) in a scattered collage. The whole cluster keeps orbiting slowly clockwise, then spirals back in, blurring blue, and merges at the centre.
scenes.build: Each card has a final (x, y) converted to polar (r, theta); angle = theta - (1-p)*80deg + orbit + exitSpin and radius = r * (0.06 + 0.94p), so one progress value spirals it out while cards stay upright. A gradient overlay's opacity = max(1 - resolve, exitP) gives the placeholder-to-screenshot resolve and the blue return.
scenes.reuse: Great for 'look what it made' or a portfolio/gallery burst: swap the images (keep about six). The polar spiral-in/out is reusable for any collage. Don't reuse the dash-* screenshots for another product.

scenes.title: Ripple rings and a blue bloom condense into the mark
scenes.summary: Two soft white rings with blue glow ripple outward from centre while a violet-blue radial bloom shrinks, and the seven-lobed gradient Codex blob comes into focus from blur, shrinking and slowly rotating inside a white halo.
scenes.build: Rings are circle divs with large blue box-shadows, sized by interpolate/glide; the blob is the CodexBlob SVG (union of circles with one gradient) with a blur prop ramp and continuous rotation. glide() keeps the shrink from stopping at keys.
scenes.reuse: A short logo-intro bridge; swap CodexBlob for your mark. It mostly sets up scene 08's spin, so pair them.

scenes.title: Logo blob writes the lines like a pen, then becomes the logo
scenes.summary: The Codex blob moves like a pen nib at the end of a centred line, writing "No complex syntax" letter by letter (letters settle from blue to ink), unwriting it right to left, then "No learning", then "No complex curve". Finally the line empties and the blob swells from 118px to 690px, sweeps its hue, stops spinning upright, and the white ">_" terminal glyph morphs in from two dots before it blurs out.
scenes.build: CHARS is a list of {ch, a (appear frame), d (disappear frame)} built by seg(); the line's left edge comes from a continuous width estimate (per-glyph Inter advance widths eased in/out) so the row glides instead of hopping as letters change. The blob gets x-only motion blur via an feGaussianBlur sized by its horizontal speed, plus a slight scaleX stretch. CodexBlob's glyphMorph animates the chevron/underscore paths.
scenes.reuse: Use for a 'no X, no Y' benefit list where the logo itself writes the copy; swap the three lines and the mark. The continuous-width centring trick is worth taking for any typed, centred line.

scenes.title: App icon over a dusk sky: "this is Codex." and tagline
scenes.summary: A looping dusk cosmos video clears from a hue-shifted blur and slowly scales down behind a white rounded app icon with the gradient blob and ">_" glyph, which settles upward. "this is Codex." rises word by word beneath it; "this is" collapses away and "Codex." grows 1.5x into a wordmark, then "Where ideas turn into code" blurs in. The whole frame blurs out at the end.
scenes.build: <Video> background with a grade interpolate (blur + hue-rotate + saturate), a radial scrim for contrast, CodexAppIcon sized/placed by glide(). "this is" sits in an inline-flex whose maxWidth shrinks to zero so "Codex." slides to centre as it scales; the tagline uses TextAnimation preset="blurIn".
scenes.reuse: A solid end-card for any product: swap the video, icon and both lines. The collapsing-prefix trick ("this is" → "Codex.") is a nice name lockup move. Don't reuse the Codex mark or name.
